canonical_data: application-defined agency, agent, and conversation-thread state saved through caller-supplied load and save callbacks
current_repo_note: Records the v1.x SDK-based framework; the README's migration guide separates it from the earlier v0.x line. It extends, and does not replace, the OpenAI Agents SDK recorded separately.
strengths: Agents talk through a dedicated send-message tool governed by explicit directional communication flows declared on the Agency, so who may delegate to whom is code rather than prompt text
Persistence is a pair of caller-supplied callbacks, so conversation threads can live in any store without a bundled database
Releases are frequent (v1.12.0 in the package manifest) and the README reports 92 percent test coverage
weaknesses: It is built on the OpenAI Agents SDK, so loop semantics, tracing, and tool format follow that dependency, and other providers arrive through an optional LiteLLM router
The v1 line is a rewrite of the v0.x framework, so older tutorials and agents need migration
Agent behaviour rests on prompt-defined roles and the chosen model; the reviewed source adds no sandbox or human-approval layer of its own beyond the SDK guardrail hooks
The README directs readers to the maintainer's paid agent-building service
why_it_matters: A widely used example of declaring multi-agent structure as directional flows over a provider SDK, rather than as free-form handoffs.
